steps.title: Position the device
steps.text: Through a 6F sheath in the right radial artery, over a 0.014-inch wire, advance the catheter with the wire about 10 cm ahead of its tip until the proximal filter, still sheathed, sits in the innominate artery. Keep the ACT above 250 s until the device is out.
steps.cue: The pigtail for the TAVR is already across the arch, curled in the non-coronary cusp.

steps.title: Pull back Slider 1
steps.text: Pull back the proximal filter slider (#1) to deploy the proximal filter in a straight stretch 1.5–2 cm past the innominate's origin. Then pull the wire fully inside the catheter.
steps.cue: The filter opens against the innominate wall, mouth toward the aorta. It can be re-sheathed and re-placed at most twice.

steps.title: Retract the rear handle slightly
steps.text: Retract the rear handle slightly to adjust the position of the articulating sheath.
steps.cue: The blue articulating sheath comes back up out of the ascending aorta toward the arch.

steps.title: Rotate Knob 2
steps.text: Rotate the articulation knob (#2) to bend the articulating sheath.

steps.title: Turn the rear handle, then wire the left carotid
steps.text: Rotate the rear handle to point the tip toward the left common carotid. Push the wire into the left carotid, no more than 5 cm.
steps.cue: The tip faces the left carotid ostium and the wire runs up the vessel.

steps.title: Retract the rear handle fully
steps.text: Retract the rear handle fully so the articulating sheath sits on the carina between the innominate and the left carotid. Adjust Knob 2 if needed so the tip points to the middle of the left carotid.
steps.cue: The sheath's U rests on the carina; its tip is just inside the left carotid.

steps.title: Advance Slider 3
steps.text: Advance the distal filter slider (#3) to deploy the distal filter 1.5–2 cm into the left carotid. Pull the wire back until it is 1 cm past the tip, and close the rear handle lock.
steps.cue: The filter opens in the left carotid, mouth toward the aorta. At most two repositions.

steps.title: During the TAVR
steps.text: The delivery catheter crosses the arch to the valve (the new valve is not drawn). Debris knocked loose from the arch wall and the valve rides the blood. The filters catch what enters the innominate and the left carotid; the left subclavian, which feeds the left vertebral artery, is not covered. At the end the pigtail comes out.
steps.cue: Debris collects toward the tip of each filter.

steps.title: Retract Slider 3
steps.text: Retract the distal filter slider (#3) to sheath the distal filter. Pull the wire fully inside the catheter.
steps.cue: The distal filter is drawn into the sheath with what it caught.

steps.title: Advance the rear handle
steps.text: Advance the rear handle to close the gap.
steps.cue: The sheath comes off the carina.

steps.title: Rotate Knob 2 back
steps.text: Rotate the articulation knob (#2) back to straighten the sheath, and push on the wire.
steps.cue: The sheath straightens and the wire leads ahead of it.

steps.title: Advance Slider 1
steps.text: Advance the proximal filter slider (#1) to sheath the proximal filter.
steps.cue: The proximal filter folds back into its sheath with its debris.

steps.title: Withdraw the device
steps.text: Withdraw the device under fluoroscopy, holding Slider 1 in place, with the wire about 10 cm ahead of the tip.
steps.cue: Everything leaves through the right subclavian.

steps.title: What the filters caught
steps.text: Outside the body, both filters can be opened again to look at what they caught.
